newsitem.title: ITALY: Bank of Italy seen assessing lira before rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Italy seen assessing lira before rate cut.

text.p: The Bank of Italy is likely to wait until December before it makes an interest rate cut, waiting to see how the lira performs within Europe's exchange rate mechanism (ERM), economists said on Monday.

The central bank, which has spent the last year building up its credibility as an inflation-buster, could use prices data due in December as a stimulus to ease rates but it will also keep a sharp eye on contract negotiations with metalworkers.

Gianluca Sanna, economist at Banco di Sardegna, said before making its next easing, which he expected to be 50 basis points, the Bank of Italy was likely to take a look at how the lira fared over the coming days.

"But if it holds up as well as it has until now there shouldn't be problems for a cut in rates by the end of the year and maybe they could take advantage from the inflation data on December 5 to cut rates," Sanna said.
The lira was close to its new 990 per mark central parity by 1330 GMT at 990.50 compared with 999 late on Friday.
The Bank of Italy last cut its key discount and fixed term advances or Lombard rates by 75 basis points to 7.5 and 9.0 percent on October 23.
Riccardo Barbieri, senior economist at Morgan Stanley in London, said he expected a 0.5-point easing soon, even between now and the release of final November CPI data on December 5.
Preliminary inflation data last week showed November CPI running at about 2.6 percent, down from October's 3.0 percent.
Ken Wattret, economist at Paribas in London, also saw the possibility of a rate cut within days due to slowing inflation.
But he pointed out the Bank of Italy had taken a very cautious approach to loosening monetary policy over the course of the past year while the rest of Europe had been easing.

"The Bank of Italy has made an explicit attempt to bolster its inflation fighting credibility. Cuts this year have been explicitly linked to inflation and the message has been drilled home that improvements in inflation dictate policy," he said.

Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio, speaking after the lira's readmittance to the ERM late on Sunday, said the exchange rate would have no implications for interest rate policy which was influenced chiefly by inflation developments.
Wattret said "That suggests the Bank of Italy may hold off until the lira has normalised and they gauge the medium term impact of ERM re-entry rather than the short term reaction."

Economists noted a third factor, beyond the lira and inflation, which might cause the Bank of Italy to pause before acting -- stalled negotiations between employers and metal and engineering unions on renewing labour contracts.

Contracts for 1.7 million metal and engineering workers expired last June but employers and unions have failed to agree new terms. Prime Minister Romano Prodi's centre-left government has said if employers do not return to the negotiating table by November 28 it will intervene to try to find a settlement.

Ilaria Fornari, economist at JP Morgan, said with 990 as the central parity, which is stronger than Italian industry wanted, "the metalworkers' contract becomes fundamental because now Italy's competitivity depends on labour costs."
She expected the central bank to wait two or three weeks before easing around 50 basis points.
